articleTitle: Systematic Literature Review on Realtime Emotion Detection Using AI Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing human business operations is an undeniable and transformative trend. This paper examines the research domain of real-time emotion detection (RED), which has seen a substantial boost in identification accuracy through advanced AI algorithms. The study involved a comprehensive survey of 202 papers, ultimately leading to the analysis of 13 key references that represent significant contributions to this field. The findings showcase the potential of RED to improve monitoring and engagement in various sectors such as security, education, healthcare, and human-machine interactions. Furthermore, the research underscores the critical role of face detection algorithms, which are essential for achieving high classification accuracy in emotion recognition tasks. Notably, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) emerged as the most widely used and effective algorithm for classifying emotions, demonstrating their value in advancing the capabilities and applications of emotion detection technologies across multiple industries.

articleTitle: SDL: Spoken Dual Learning for Joint Optimization of SLU and SLG
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel spoken dual learning (SDL) frame-work aimed at the concurrent training of spoken language understanding (SLU) and generation (SLG) models. The central proposition is to consider SLU and SLG as conditional text generation tasks steered by prompts, thereby offering consistent goals and context-aware direction. SDL navigates the inherent dual task constraints through an innovative transformation technique utilizing noisy transcripts and intents. The blueprint of SDL incorporates high-profile, pre-trained speech models such as Wav2vec2 or Whisper, serving as the backbone. Extensive experimentation on datasets of varying sizes (small, medium, and large) provides empirical evidence demonstrating that SDL exhibits higher performance levels compared to models that are independently trained, as the cycle consistency of mapping be-tween speech, semantics, and text acts as effective regularization.

articleTitle: Modification of K-Means Clustering Algorithm for Optimizing School Zoning System Using Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The increasing complexity of school zoning systems due to population growth and uneven geographic distribution has created significant challenges in ensuring balanced and fair allocation of students. This research focuses on modifying the K-Means clustering algorithm to optimize school zoning using Big Data. The admission of new students through the zoning system in Indonesia is crucial for enhancing access to quality education without discrimination. However, the current grouping process does not consider the distance between students' homes and schools. Clustering algorithms offer a solution by organizing data while accounting for the proximity between cluster members and their centroids. K-means clustering has shown promising results in grouping similar data but has limitations in determining centroid values, which can lead to suboptimal clustering. The modified K-Means algorithm is designed to address the limitations of traditional clustering methods in handling unbalanced group sizes, ensuring that each school zone has a proportional number of students. This study develops a clustering algorithm with fixed centroids to balance the number of members in each cluster. These algorithms are evaluated by calculating the total distance of each cluster member to its centroid. The proposed algorithms effectively cluster data and balance cluster membership, making them suitable for student placement in the zoning system. This research aims to provide a more effective solution for school zoning that can be applied to real-world educational systems, ultimately improving the fairness and efficiency of student distribution across schools.

articleTitle: Security of Electric Vehicles: A Brief Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are quickly becoming a critical part of the global transportation system. While they offer many benefits, they also introduce various cybersecurity risks that must be addressed. This paper examines the security challenges associated with EVs, charging infrastructure, and communication protocols. It reviews the existing literature, analyzes potential threats, and discusses possible countermeasures to ensure the safe and reliable operation of EVs and their integration into the smart grid.

articleTitle: Adoption Tea Leaf Disease Detection Using ResNet50 and Advance Hyperparameter
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Advanced technology has become a key factor in managing plant diseases. One effective approach to diagnosing plant diseases is the use of deep learning models within the field of image processing. Tea leaf disease is one such condition that demands rapid and efficient intervention. This study employs a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture, specifically ResNet-50 and Inception V3, to classify six different diseases affecting tea leaves. To enhance the performance of ResNet-50 and Inception V3, data augmentation techniques were incorporated into the training process to increase data variability, and hyperparameters were fine-tuned to improve model effectiveness. The research includes four experimental scenarios aimed at achieving optimal outcomes. Three of these scenarios involve adjusting hyperparameters such as the optimizer, learning rate, and batch size. Classification was performed using three sets of data augmentation methods: zoom, rotation, and flip; zoom, rotation, and shear; and zoom, rotation, and shift. Fine-tuning hyperparameters and applying the right data augmentation techniques significantly improved ResNet-50's performance. The final results revealed that ResNet-50 outperformed the other models in classifying tea leaf diseases, achieving an average accuracy of 98.30% with the Adam optimizer, a learning rate of 0.0001, a batch size of 16, and the augmentation techniques of rotation, zoom, and flip.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Memory Overclocking on the Performance of AMD Athlon 200GE
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: In contemporary times, individuals increasingly utilize computers to facilitate their tasks, while others employ them for gaming purposes. AMD has introduced a processor, the AMD Athlon 200GE, which provides high performance and efficiency at a relatively affordable price. The Athlon™ 200GE delivers 11% faster performance for 3D graphics rendering compared to the previous 7th Gen AMD A12-9800 APU processor and 19% faster than competing processors in its class. The Athlon 200GE is specifically designed for users with budget constraints who still wish to engage in gaming activities. This research aims to determine the optimal memory configuration to enhance the gaming performance of the AMD Athlon 200GE processor, specifically when running Grand Theft Auto V (GTA V). The findings suggest that targeted memory overclocking can significantly improve gaming experiences, with an 11.7% increase in average FPS achieved through memory frequency adjustments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Early Diagnosis and Precise Classification of Type 2 Diabetes with Diabetic Retinopathy Using Machine Learning and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The paper describes an accurate classification of Type 2 Diabetes with Diabetic Retinopathy using Machine Learning and Image Processing. The objective of the paper is to find Diabetic Retinopathy from the image of retina whether a patient has the disease if yes, is it on the first stage, moderate or severe stage. The Dataset used in the study are Diabetic Retinopathy, Aptot2019 _blindness detection and Messidor2. The research shows the comparison between CNN models, including Xception, Alex Net, VggNet-s, VggNet-16, and ResN et-50. The ResN et-50 shows better performance than other models. The research ensured 96 % accuracy, and the value of precision is 0.97 from the proposed but it can be increased by improving the model. The study shows an excellent result with deep learning but there can be more improvement in the quality of images and fine-tuning by using other optimal technics.

articleTitle: Analysis of Round-Robin and Random Scheduling Algorithms on Sensor Node Activation Towards Latency of Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: A Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) is a network system consisting of wireless sensor nodes that collect and transmit data. One crucial factor that affects WSN performance is latency, which is the time required to send data to the gateway. High latency can cause data delivery delays, resulting in data becoming irrelevant. At the same time, receiving real-time data quickly is the primary monitoring method. In addition, high latency can cause greater energy consumption because the sensor node device must be active longer. One way to overcome latency is to implement traffic management techniques such as scheduling data delivery or using priority delivery methods, which can reduce congestion and latency. This paper discusses the effect of latency on WSN using scheduling algorithms, namely Round-Robin and Random scheduling. The results were then taken 30 times to obtain a statistical comparison. The results obtained in the experiment received a Round-Robin scheduling algorithm that was superior to the random scheduling algorithm with a mean and standard deviation value of 12.68 and 2.33, respectively.

articleTitle: Diabetic Retinopathy Detection using Convolutional Neural Networks on Retinal Fundus Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The importance of early and standardized detection of diabetic retinopathy as one of the major causes of blindness to diabetic patients is proposed within the work using convolutional neural network. The paper proposes deep learning methodology that is compared and proposed the best configuration of its hidden layers' configuration, activation function, optimization algorithm and input layer parameters. The work was trained and tested on a medium size of retinal fundus imaging (inside surface of the eye) images to classify the present of retinopathy with robustness and promising mean accuracy of 92% in several generations of epochs. It describes optimum configuration of the adjusted deep learning algorithm's hyperparameters in solving the adversity of the case to recognize early symptoms retinopathy. The study as well contributes to the advancement of imaging technology in the domain of ophthalmology by adopting machine learning and computer vision to support further medical justification, learning process and remote medical support.

articleTitle: Memory Management and Arbitration for Multi-Channel Duplex Communication on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Memory is an essential resource while implementing computationally intensive applications on the Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). When IP cores with high performance are utilized to implement external interfaces with large data rates and reliable communication link, memory is a critical resource for addressing data transfer and bandwidth requirements. Memory controller in general supports DDR2/DDR3/DDR4 SDRAM. When memory is shared between various modules of design, the memory controller has to be utilized effectively to cater for the bandwidth requirements for all modules. This paper discusses the conflict cases, management and arbitration of memory implemented with FPGA in a scenario where a core is implemented to bridge between two high speed interfaces. In which one of this interface is communicating with external environment in multiple channel configuration. It covers the information regarding hardware involved, IP cores implemented in FPGA for the communication channels data buffering, PCIe bus arbitration and effective throughput in the transfer.

articleTitle: The Development of Chicken Disease Detection Application Using the Xception Transfer Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Chicken farming in Indonesia is a potential business, considering the high demand for chicken meat and eggs. However, this business also has a significant risk of loss due to diseases that often attack chickens. This problem leads this research to find a solution so farmers can reduce the risk of loss and handle chicken diseases more effectively. To answer this challenge, we develop an application specifically designed to help chicken farmers recognize various types of chicken diseases and the symptoms that appear and recommend preventive and treatment actions. This application also has a direct disease detection feature that allows farmers to get recommendations for the right medicine and the nearest purchase location. To develop the application, we use the Xception Transfer Learning Method. Xception is a deep learning model developed by Google to improve the Inception architecture, tailored explicitly for computer vision tasks like image classification and object detection by reducing the number of parameters, making the model more efficient without losing accuracy. The testing result shows that by utilizing transfer learning, the model successfully accurately classified various types of chicken diseases based on feces images. This application is expected to be an effective tool for farmers to minimize the risk of loss and maintain the health of their livestock, especially in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Data-Driven State of Health Estimation of Lithium-ion Battery Cells Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Many battery cells are being degraded once it is used for a period of time. Most battery cells can only show the State of Charge (SoC) of the battery when it is being charged. However, the battery cells do not have the same capacity as when they are new. Thus, knowing the State of Health (SoH) of a battery is a must. There are many machine learning methods that can be used to estimate the SoH of the battery, such as Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Regression, and Neural Network. These methods are being compared in this study based on the mean absolute error (MAE) of the methods. This study uses data-driven to estimate the SoH using four different machine learning methods. This study shows 0.05 for the MAE for battery cell Li-on 18650 and 0.02 MAE for battery cell Li-ion 21700. Both MAE for Li-ion 18650 and Li-ion 21700 uses RF method as the best prediction model.

articleTitle: Development and Analysis of Autonomous Vision System for Nuclear Reactor Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The paper introduces an advanced vision system that aims to do maintenance of nuclear reactors that require high precision and safety. The development enables to work in high-radiation environments and de-risk radiation exposure to workers. A vision system-based autonomous robotic system aims to enhance safety, reliability, efficiency, and accuracy in nuclear reactor maintenance tasks. This System enables and facilitates real-time monitoring and identification to perform a wide range of operations. The system will be integrated with advanced vision algorithms and machine learning techniques to operate robotic systems for efficient and accurate results. The system can be utilized through severe tests and simulations for efficient and precise fail-safe recognition, fault identification, and investigation tasks in hazardous radiation environments. The vision system-based robotic system can be used for advanced nuclear reactor manufacturing and development. The system could be used for autonomous nuclear waste disposal systems.

articleTitle: Detection of Tuberculosis Based on X-Ray Image Using the Vision Transformer Method
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Tuberculosis, or TB, is an infectious disease caused by the Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacteria, which can attack the human body regardless of age and gender. This bacterium is a very strong bacillus, requiring a long time to treat. The types of radiological examinations commonly used today to detect tuberculosis are chest X-rays and CT scans. However, not all hospitals have CT scan machines due to their higher cost, while almost every hospital has an X-ray machine. This research aims to develop an assistive device with a high level of accuracy in detecting the disease through the analysis of X-ray images. The solution is to develop a tuberculosis detection assistive device based on X-ray images using the Vision Transformer classification model. The dataset used is obtained from four references and contains chest X-ray images categorized into four classes: Normal, Tuberculosis, Pneumonia, and Covid-19. This Vision Transformer model is designed to classify chest X-ray images to predict lung diseases according to the specified labels. From this research, the model can predict with an accuracy of up to 89%. The result of this research can help doctors in making decisions and also serve as a learning tool for detecting diseases in X-ray images.

articleTitle: Stock Buy and Sell Predictions Based on Technical Analysis and News Sentiment Using Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The fluctuations in stock market prices are a compelling subject for examination due to their significant profit potential. Market participants utilize stock transaction data and its derivatives, such as technical analysis indicators, to forecast stock prices. Sometimes technical analysis is combined with stock news sentiment to strengthen predictions. An automated system is required for more objective and expedited results due to the subjectivity of technical analysis predictions and news sentiment. Therefore, this study aims to develop a stock buy and sell prediction model by combining historical data and news sentiment. The technical analysis indicators used are: Bollinger Bands (BB), Exponential Moving Average (EMA), Simple Moving Average (SMA), Relative Strength Index (RSI), and Moving Average Convergence/Divergence (MACD). News data is categorized into positive, negative, or neutral sentiment. The fusion of historical data and news sentiment is used for buy and sell prediction input with random forest. The results of buy and sell predictions with random forest are compared with other methods, namely SVM and LSTM. The results show that the proposed method, random forest, gets an accuracy of 80.74%, better than SVM and LSTM.

articleTitle: Optimizing ANN Architecture for Classifying Student Stress Levels
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Classifying students' stress levels is very important in the world of education. For this reason, this research proposes an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) architectural optimization process to classify students' stress levels by comparing the performance of three optimizers: Ranger, Adam, and Adagrad. Optimization is carried out by exploring variations in hyperparameter values such as learning rate, regularization, number of neurons in hidden layers 1 and 2, and epoch. Model performance testing is carried out using evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-Score, and AUC. This research also explores the effects of oversampling using SMOTE-N and the effect of adding hidden layers of up to three layers. The results show that the Adam optimizer with SMOTE-N using two hidden layers produces the best model. Ablation studies were conducted to understand the influence of each hyperparameter, showing that regulation and hidden layers play an important role in avoiding overfitting and improving model performance.

articleTitle: Proof of Federated Learning Contribution (PoFLC) for Secure Agri-Data Sharing and Collaborative Model Training
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The proliferation of heterogeneous agricultural devices generates vast amounts of data, necessitating secure and efficient methods for decentralized training and data sharing. Traditional centralized approaches face significant challenges concerning data privacy, security, and scalability. This paper introduces a novel consensus mechanism called Proof of Federated Learning Contribution (PoFLC) within a secure multi-chain framework designed for agri-data sharing and collaborative model training. PoFLC quantifies the contributions of participating devices based on model update quality, reliability, and resources. Integrating federated learning with blockchain technology ensures data privacy while enhancing model performance in a decentralized environment. Extensive experiments on agricultural datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of PoFLC in maintaining data confidentiality, achieving consensus efficiently, and improving the accuracy of collaborative models trained on agri-data.

articleTitle: Conceptual for Game Development Design with Facial Expressions
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The balance of playing skills and challenges is an important factor in keeping the engagement of players in a game. Therefore, video game developers are required to consider the challenges given to players. Game design has a role in motivating players and ensuring that they have responsibilities. This research focuses on analysing players' experiences obtained from the players' emotions and giving the data to the game developers for evaluation and improvement on several points. Typically, developers use surveys to get feedback for that scene; however, for video game improvement, developers need to know the players' real expressions while playing the game. In this work, we aim to survey player expression to provide a complete overview of the state of research on game design. We implemented a facial expression detector in a game to analyse players' emotions. The data of “Disgust” and “Happy” expressions were obtained from the experiment and provided to game developers for game improvement. Despite the outcome not matching our expectations, from the perspective of video game development, the proposed method is beneficial for improvement evaluation in game design development.

articleTitle: Application of Dynamic Time Warping for Clustering Cellular Data Traffic Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The demand for internet access has been increasing every year. According to data from the Indonesia Central Bureau of Statistics in 2022, there has been a significant rise since 2018, with the percentage of the population accessing the internet growing substantially. Cellular operators, as Internet Service Providers (ISP), need to analyze internet consumption within their networks, one of which is data traffic. Data traffic, typically measured in Bytes, is a measure for network productivity and has a direct impact on a company's business. The higher the network's data traffic consumption, the greater the potential revenue for cellular operators. Failure to analyze the patterns can result in serious consequences for cellular operators, including network capacity planning failures, a decline in customer expe-rience performance, and not optimal revenue. Therefore, cellular operators need to analyze data traffic consumption to understand the potential and behavior of their users. Unfortunately, data traffic consumption has characteristics which fluctuate over time, depending on user behavior. These characteristics present challenges for operators, operators require a method which can learn traffic data patterns in the time domain. In this study, a data traffic pattern analysis will be conducted using time-series clustering methods to analyze data traffic in 61 districts from one of the cellular operators in Indonesia. By utilizing the Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) algorithm, this study aims to identify the characteristics of each cluster based on pattern similarities. The characteristics of each cluster will highlight potential data traffic consumption according to specific time conditions in the selected districts.

articleTitle: Comparison of Classification Algorithm In Sentiment Analysis of E-Commerce App Comments Based on Feature Extraction and Imbalanced Handling Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has significantly changed consumer habits, offering previously unheard-of accessibility and convenience. A massive amount of user-generated content, such as reviews and comments, was produced. Sentiment analysis has advanced, but several problems remain. One major issue was the imbalance in user reviews, where a positive comment is more than a negative comment. The proposed goal was to compare the performance of a classification algorithm that applied feature extraction and overs amp ling to the sentiment analysis of comments written on e-commerce apps. The dataset was taken from Google Plays about e-commerce, with 1500 data in Indonesian comments and ratings. Based on the results, both the Overs amp ling (SMOTE) and undersampling techniques as imbalanced handling methods can enhance the test accuracy of all algorithms like Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Naive Bayes (NB), Random Forests (RF), and Support Vector Machines (SVM) models using TF-IDF as feature extraction. The results suggest that Rus outperformed SMOTE in ANN, NB, and SVM accuracy by around 85%, 85%, and 84.6%, respectively. In contrast, Smote boosted the RF model by 80.8%. Overall, The NB model has boosted accuracy testing by roughly 8%, while imbalance data (76.67%) has grown to 85%.

articleTitle: Enhance Covid-19 Detection Using Inception and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Covid-19 was first discovered in Wuhan, a province in China in early 2020. This disease has a very powerful spread. Covid-19 disease will attack the lungs and cause pneumonia. Even many cases in the world cause death. Detecting Covid-19 using x-ray images is a very important method because it is inexpensive, the tools used are widely available in almost all hospitals or clinics. The use of deep learning algorithms in detecting Covid-19 is an effort that has been widely developed by researchers. Deep learning functions to automatically study data to distinguish types of lung diseases including Covid-19. However, several previous studies have addressed problems in detection that still contain detection errors. This study aims to develop an algorithm model based on Inception and Attention to produce more effective Covid-19 disease detection results. In this study, the use of a combination of the Inception and Attention algorithms succeeded in increasing accuracy by 0.96 based on testing using metric evaluations, namely accuracy tests, F1, recall, precision and confusion matrices and Area Under Curve (AUC). Compared with several studies using several types of deep learning, the combination of Inception and Attention successfully increases the effectiveness of classification results.

articleTitle: Time-Delay Compensation in Robotic Arms: A Novel Control Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Time delay is an important factor in control systems, particularly in robotic applications that involve feedback loops, remote control, and networked systems. In these situations, delays can have a substantial effect on the performance of the system, resulting in reduced accuracy of control, instability, or inadequate tracking of the trajectory. This work describes the application of MATLAB Simulink to design and simulate a Time Delay Control (TDC) system for the Universal Robots UR5 robot. The TDC system is designed to ensure consistent and uniform trajectory tracking. A unique control approach is implemented into a dynamic model of the UR5 robot to ensure efficient time delays and system stability under control. The control strategy considers the time delays that naturally arise in robotic systems and, by using Time Delay Estimation (TDE), it adapts control interventions in real-time to ensure precise and smooth control. The present study focuses on the design of the controller, specifically examining the construction of the model to accurately represent the physical characteristics of the UR5 robot and the control's ability to mitigate delays. The integration of real-time feedback and predictive techniques enables the TDC system to adjust to variations in delay, so guaranteeing dependable performance across diverse operational situations. Validation of the proposed system's effectiveness is achieved by simulation results that demonstrate its resilience under various delay conditions. These findings indicate that the TDC system retains stability and accuracy, even under substantial time delays. The system's resilience is readily apparent in its capacity to consistently attain precise trajectory tracking, demonstrating its potential for practical integration in real-world robotic applications where delays are inevitable.

articleTitle: Performance of LORA Gateway MQTT Protocol Communication on Motor Cycle IoT-Based: A QoS Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: In IoT-based systems that utilize platforms for data exchange, reliable and efficient communication methods are essential to enable users to search for and monitor system data. Similarly, in IoT -based motorcycle security protection systems, dependable communication methods are crucial. LoRa and the MQTT protocol serve as solutions for data communication in the IoT system implemented in this research. To evaluate the reliability of the system's communication, tests were conducted under LOS (Line of Sight) and NLOS (Non-Line of Sight) conditions, with optimal transmission ranges of 500 meters for LOS and 300–325 meters for NLOS. The analysis was based on test parameters, including a delay of 122.25 ms, a throughput of 66.75 bps, and a packet loss rate of 1.5%. The LoRa testing across different ranges yielded RSSI values of -115 to -71 dBm under LOS conditions and -122 to -52 dBm under NLOS conditions. These test parameter results for LoRa and MQTT communication fall into the excellent category with a high SF 12 value. Additionally, the Telegram Bot platform was successfully integrated into the motorcycle security protection system, enabling remote control and monitoring. Notifications and data from sensor nodes are received by users through the Telegram Bot, demonstrating the system's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Real Time Air Pollutant Forecast Using Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Indoor air pollution poses a hidden threat affecting our health and well-being. Evaluating the indoor environment's air quality is necessary to minimize the risk caused by air pollution. Previous research has explored machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques like ARIMA, Prophet, and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) for pollution prediction using pre-recorded data, leaving real-time forecasting unaddressed. This paper compares ARIMA, Prophet, MLP, and Staked models, combining all three models to evaluate the best model for forecasting air quality with collected datasets and real-time data and integrating the Internet of Things device with the Raspberry Pi Pico and MQ 135 sensor. Using metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), R2 Score, and time taken to train and forecast, evaluate models to determine whether they are suitable for live predictions. The result shows that the MLP model managed to get the best evaluation score on the available dataset at 2.5 MAE, 8.7 MSE, 2.95 RMSE, and 0.98 R2 Score. Despite the Prophet model shows an inferior metrics score compared to the MLP, it is considered suitable for live predictions because of its significantly faster training time of 0.08 seconds and forecasting time of 0.05 seconds. The Prophet model also predicts its lower bound and upper bound, enhancing its generalization capability. The prophet model generally predicts within its prediction bounds with 75% accuracy on the available dataset and 85% on the live dataset.

articleTitle: Utilizing Machine Learning Techniques to Identify Anomalies in Financial Transactions for Laos Banking
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Recently, rapid technological advancements have sparked the growth and widespread adoption of new financial industries. This includes internet-based services such as applications, credit cards, ATMs, online shopping payments, and online money transfers. As these systems become more sophisticated, the risks and threats also increase significantly. This research aims to explore ways to protect the assets of customers and banks in Laos from falling victim to individuals with malicious intent who attempt to fraudulently steal customer assets online. New technologies, like creating anomaly detection models for financial transactions, safeguard customer and bank assets by filtering out suspicious activities before confirming the actual transaction. If the system detects an anomaly in a transaction, it will alert the account holder and ask for confirmation before proceeding with the transaction. We trained the anomaly detection model on a dataset of over 12 million records, utilizing techniques like isolation forest (IF), local outlier factor (LOF), and autoencoder (AE). We assessed the effectiveness of these three models, obtaining ROC scores of IF = 0.54, LOF = 0.50, and AE = 0.92, as well as training times (in minutes) of IF = 3.37, LOF = 17.42, and AE = 8.57. The AE model was shown to be the most successful in detecting anomalies, indicating that it might be used as an API to improve the monitoring of financial transactions. Additionally, the lack of labeled data, which is typical in fraud detection tasks, was handled via the use of unsupervised learning. But because training AE needed a significant amount of computing power, the study was constrained, which would have affected its viability for real-time applications.

articleTitle: Common Modulus Attack on the Elliptic Curve-Based RSA Algorithm Variant
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This paper investigates the vulnerability of elliptic curve-based RSA to the common modulus attack, a well-known cryptanalytic method. RSA is a commonly utilized public-key encryption system that is based on the challenge of factoring large composite numbers, securing digital signatures, key exchanges, and data transmission. The security of the RSA algorithm has been thoroughly analyzed and continues to be robust against numerous types of attacks. However, in 2023, Boudabra and Nitaj introduced a variant of RSA employing elliptic curves within the ring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$</tex>, aiming to enhance both security and efficiency. Despite these advancements, this paper demonstrates that the common modulus attack can still compromise the system. By leveraging a shared modulus in multiple encryptions, the attack successfully recovers the plaintext without requiring the trapdoor information. We conduct simulations using specific parameters, with exponents <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e_{1} = 233, e_{2} = 151$</tex>, and modulus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n = 181603559630213323475279432919469869812801$</tex>, showing how the attack is feasible even for elliptic curve-based RSA. The results indicate that elliptic curve-enhanced RSA, while improving efficiency, remains susceptible to the common modulus attack. Our findings underscore the importance of careful implementation strategies and the need for greater attention to this vulnerability in practical cryptographic applications.

articleTitle: Pure-inTention x G.I.: Purpose-driven Trip Demand Estimation Framework Considering Multi-dimensional Geospatial Information*
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This study offers a crucial contribution at the intersection of social science and emerging technology, presenting a multidisciplinary framework to address post-pandemic challenges in urban mobility. By integrating multi-dimensional geospatial data with dynamic datasets, we introduce a novel framework designed to monitor and classify various trip purposes. Experimental results show the influence of differing social distancing policies on local movement patterns at the district level, revealing essential insights into regional trip purpose variations and their socio-economic impacts. To implement this multi-dimensional geospatial approach, we utilized diverse machine learning and deep learning techniques, alongside optimization strategies, to analyze data from multiple sources-credit card transactions, geodemographic profiles, traffic counts, local business data, and surveyed origin-destination flows. Techniques like Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP), K-means clustering, Random Forest, and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) were applied, with Tabu Search and Hill Climbing strategies for optimization. The well-trained prediction model developed in this study demonstrated accurate performance in understanding traffic patterns and their consequential trip purposes. The experiment results revealed the extent of the pandemic's impact across districts and their sensitivities to different policies. The developed framework proves beneficial not only for individual districts and stakeholders but also for comprehensive county and national strategic planning.

articleTitle: Comparison Study of Preprocessing Methods for Corporate Loan Default Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The probability of default (PD) in corporate loans refers to the likelihood that a borrower will fail to meet their debt obligations within a specified time frame. Macroeconomic conditions, including factors such as economic growth, interest rates, inflation, and unemployment rates, directly influence the financial health of corporations, impacting their ability to meet debt obligations and thus affecting the probability of default in corporate loans. The challenge in predicting the probability of default using macroeconomic conditions is the dynamic and interconnected nature of the economy, making it difficult to accurately forecast how various factors will evolve. Due to this obstacle, it is essential to perform a comprehensive literature review to understand the existing methodologies and approaches used in PD prediction. By reviewing a range of studies, the strengths and weaknesses of different approaches have been identified. This literature review yielded 22 primary papers examined, indicating differences in methods used to achieve higher accuracy levels focusing on feature selection and engineering rather than fine-tuning and modifying machine learning methods. Some feature selection methods used to improve accuracy include using multi-period cumulative data on macroeconomics, handling dataset imbalance with SMOTE or Kolmogorov-Smirnov, and clustering macroeconomic variables. The preprocessing pipeline integrating stationarity testing, correlation analysis, and clustering has been implemented to enhance machine learning model performance and interpretability. Experimental findings highlighted XGBoost's highest predictive accuracy, 0.986, affirming the efficacy of advanced preprocessing and clustering-based feature engineering for optimizing model performance in practical applications.

articleTitle: Text Summarization of Batak Toba Language Using Bidirectional Auto-Regressive Transformers Model
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This developed an automatic text summarization system for the Batak Toba language using the Bidirectional Auto-Regressive Transformers (BART) model. The system aims to simplify lengthy Batak language texts, making them more accessible and understandable for readers, especially those frequently engaging with Batak language content. To ensure summarization accuracy, the model was also trained on a dataset specific to Batak language contexts, allowing it to effectively capture linguistic nuances. During development, the system utilized natural language processing (NLP) techniques to process data. The data used in this study is not updated in real-time, making performance dependent on manually updated datasets. The research methodology includes dataset collection from various sources, data preprocessing, model training, model testing, and performance evaluation using ROUGE metrics. Model evaluation yielded F1 scores of 0.8437 for ROUGE-1, 0.8065 for ROUGE-2, and 0.8437 for ROUGE-L, indicating that the developed system successfully produces coherent text summaries. For further development, expanding the dataset and improving model quality are recommended to support more optimal text summarization that meets user needs.

articleTitle: Mapping and Prediction of Stunting Potential Using K-Means Clustering and Support Vector Regression (Case Study of Palopo City)
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This research uses the K-Means algorithm to group cases of stunting and the Support Vector Regression (SVR) algorithm to forecast stunting patterns in Palopo City. Data from 9 districts was analyzed using K-Means clustering to find areas with high and low risk of stunting. The analysis showed a Silhouette score of 0.63 for cluster = 2, suggesting distinct groups. The optimized SVR model, using GridSearchCV, predicted 159 TB/U Short cases and 78.6 TB/U Very Short cases for 2024, with a combined total of 237.65 stunting cases. Evaluation metrics indicated that there were low error rates, with Mean Absolute Percentage Errors (MAPE) of 6% and 19% for TB/U Short and TB/U Very Short, respectively. Furthermore, the system evaluates a child's nutritional health by determining their height-for-age Z-score. If stunting is identified, the system offers practical suggestions for prompt intervention and care. This study provides a scalable model for reducing stunting, allowing policymakers to distribute resources efficiently and execute focused health initiatives.

articleTitle: Cryptanalysis of the RSA Cryptosystem Based on $n$ Prime Numbers
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: As digital platforms become essential in daily life, the demand for robust information security has grown. Cryptography, particularly RSA, plays a central role in safeguarding sensitive data. In response to vulnerabilities in RSA, the modified RSA cryptosystem (MRSA), based on multiple prime numbers, was introduced. This study analyzes MRSA's resilience against attacks, employing techniques like Pollard's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> - 1 factorization, the common modulus attack, and the cycling attack. Our results have shown that Pollard's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> - 1 attack is faster when applied to factorize the integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> in MRSA compared to RSA. Additionally, common modulus attacks, multiplicative properties attacks, and cycling attacks can be used to cryptanalyze MRSA in polynomial time. This research highlights MRSA's limitations, suggesting that simply increasing the number of prime factors does not guarantee stronger security.

articleTitle: An IoT Pen-Liked Screening Device Characterizations in Tissue Structures of Mouth Cavity Organ
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This research presents design and analysis of a monopole antenna for early oral cancer detection. An operating frequency of ISM (Industrial, Scientific and Medical) at 2.45 GHz, the antenna was simulated to assess its electromagnetic wave interaction with human body tissues. The antenna with dimensions of 27.65 mm in length and 3.00 mm in diameter, showed favorable performance. VSWR (Voltage Standing Wave Ratio) value of 1.57 dB, a return loss value of −13.01 dB, and a gain value of 3.389 dBi in simulations. Fabrication results demonstrated an improved VSWR of 1.01 dB and a significant return loss of −49.0 dB, with a gain of 21.65 dBi. The simulations also investigated the antenna's behavior within the oral cavity, revealing a decrease in gain and an increase in power loss density, demonstrating the effects of body tissue on electromagnetic wave propagation. These findings emphasize the antenna's potential for practical applications in oral cancer detection, while also highlighting challenges due to signal attenuation caused by human tissue. The research aims to contribute to the development of effective, non-invasive health monitoring systems for early disease detection, particularly in oncology.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning in Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Transfer learning has been a game-changer for natural language processing (NLP), and this technique has massively accelerated progress in the field of NLP, specifically by substantially benefiting from advancements being made elsewhere. We evaluated their performance economic model on a set of tasks and found they outperformed generic transformer models in accuracy as well as generalization. This is also a reminder of the importance of large-scale pretraining, which requires less task-specific data and consequently facilitates faster model development. To achieve a better understanding of the impact on model performance from fine-tuning, combined with datasets characteristics and architecture details. They demonstrated that transfer learning models not only increase classification accuracy in various fields, ranging from healthcare to legal document analysis but also vastly improve the efficiency. These results have important implications, they extend transfer learning from being merely a trend in NLP to something truly necessary for making progress on several fundamental task of NLP. However, work is not done on model interpretability and extending these improvements to low resource languages. This suggests future research in operationalizing these powerful tools transparently and fairly across a wide range of linguistic and cultural contexts. We hope that it can help, at least in some way, to grow the community interested on learning more about how these models work so effectively and guide them toward using transfer learning wherever valuable.

articleTitle: Honey in Depth: A Multi-Layered Deception Framework for Internet of Things Security
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The digitalization of modern life has brought unprecedented convenience, yet cybersecurity remains a persistent challenge. As the frequency and sophistication of cyberattacks increase, it has become evident that proactive defense measures alone are insufficient. This paper introduces Honey-in-Depth, a novel lightweight system that leverages the concept of deception-in-depth to enhance cybersecurity. By deploying honey tokens across multiple layers of defense, Honey-in-Depth provides a comprehensive approach to deceive and confine intruders. We implement and evaluate the system on Ubuntu, demonstrating its potential applicability to IoT devices running Linux distributions. Our results show that Honey-in-Depth effectively alerts on unauthorized access while imposing minimal overhead on system resources. The system achieved a 100% detection rate for honey token interactions, a 0% false positive rate, and less than a 5% increase in system resource usage. This approach offers a promising solution to bolster security posture through deception techniques, particularly in resource constrained IoT environments. The study contributes to the evolving field of deception-based cybersecurity, offering valuable insights for enhancing modern security strategies in an increasingly complex threat landscape.

articleTitle: Multi-Extraction Techniques of Content-Based Music Recommender System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of music rec-ommendation in the digital age, where the diversity of user preferences necessitates an effective filtering method. Traditional approaches like collaborative filtering struggle with new users due to a lack of item history, and content-based methods often rely solely on textual attributes like lyrics and genres, neglecting the rich information within audio files. Previous works have been limited by a narrow set of music feature extraction techniques. In contrast, this research leverages a multi-extraction approach to enhance recommendation accuracy by utilizing six distinct audio feature extraction methods-MFCC, zero crossing rate, spectral centroid, spectral bandwidth, spectral roll-off, and chroma STFT. Cosine similarity is used to determine the similarity between audio files. Utilizing the FMA dataset and evaluating the system with the NDCG method, the study achieves a notable score of 0.957, demonstrating the high relevance of the music recommendations provided. This multi-extraction technique approach represents a significant advancement in audio-based music recommendation systems.

articleTitle: HAN-CapsNet: Multi-polarity Based Sentiment Classification using Hierarchical Attention Networks and Capsule Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Aspect-based Sentiment classification intends to find sentiment polarity towards a particular aspect becoming a significant task for sentiment analysis. Conventional techniques obtained satisfactory outcomes, yet they mainly focused on utilizing local structure information of the given sentence, like syntactical dependency limitations in a sentence. To solve this issue, the Hierarchical Attention Networks-Capsule Neural Network (HAN-CapsNet) is proposed for multi-polarity based sentiment classification. Initially, BERT tokenization is performed using an input text from a database. The second task considers BiLSTM for Multi-Word Aspect Term (MWAT) extraction. Later, feature extraction is done where the extracted features are statistical, count vectorization, emoticons, hashtags, all caps, elongated units, negation, bag-of-units, syntactic n-gram features, and contextual features. Finally, MWAT-based polarity sentiment classification is accomplished by utilizing HAN-CapsNet. The BiLSTM outperforms previous feature extraction algorithms with an accuracy rise of 3% - 6%. Moreover, the performance measures of the proposed model for sentiment classification, like Accuracy, True Positive Rate, and True Negative Rate show significant improvements over the baseline models.

articleTitle: Human-Centred Interfaces on Engineering Teleoperation: A Case Study of Utilising Virtual Reality (VR) with Robotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Human-machine interface (HMI) focuses on developing user interfaces (UI) where humans interact with digital systems. As the prevalence of robots in industrial settings increases, the complexity of human-robot interaction becomes increasingly critical. Designing intuitive and effective interfaces is essential to ensure robotic systems' safe and efficient operation. This paper explores the use of virtual reality (VR) as a human-centred interface for engineering teleoperation, focusing on the core functions of industrial robot teach pendants. We aim to develop a general VR-based robotic manipulator interface by analysing existing HMI and identifying potential VR enhancements. Our results suggest that VR-based interfaces have the potential to improve user experience (UX), efficiency, accuracy, and UI/UX design flexibility. This work intends to contribute to the VR teleoperation concept for other robotic systems like drones/unmanned aerial vehicles, autonomous underwater vehicles, and automated guided vehicles.

articleTitle: The Power of Context: A Comparative Analysis of Text Embeddings in Radiology Report Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: In radiology report generation, the representation of medical language is crucial for producing accurate and meaningful descriptions of imaging findings. However, accurately capturing and representing complex medical language and imaging findings remains a significant challenge. The variability in radiology report structures, specialized medical terminology, and the need for precise contextual understanding complicate the automated generation of high-quality reports. While recent advancements in natural language processing (NLP) have introduced powerful text embeddings, it remains unclear which of these methods best addresses the unique demands of radiological language. This study aims to address this gap by conducting a comparative analysis of several prominent text embedding techniques, including BERT, BioBERT, clinicalBERT, and BioGPT, to understand their effectiveness in generating radiology reports. We employ a framework that integrates image features extracted from Vision Transformer (ViT) with contextualized text embeddings, followed by Long Short Term Memory Network (LSTM) decoder and Generative Pre-Trained Transformer 2 (GPT -2) decoder for report generation. Our experiments reveal that BioGPT outperforms other embeddings, demonstrating a superior ability to capture complex medical concepts and provide coherent description up to 20% better than other embedding models in both LSTM and GPT-2 decoder. These findings highlight the importance of selecting appropriate text embeddings for optimizing the quality and clinical relevance of automated radiology report generation.

articleTitle: Phonics Recognition Using Machine Learning with MFCC Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Phonics is an educational method designed to help children decode written letters and spoken sounds, ultimately aiding in reading proficiency. Currently, there is no research on Phonics alphabet recognition. Thus, this research explores the application of Machine Learning techniques for recognizing Phonics alphabet spelling, utilizing Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) for feature extraction, known for its effectiveness in speech recognition. The research employs classifiers such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), and Random Forest, incorporating data augmentation techniques like random and constant noise addition and time shifting, with MFCC extraction performed both manually and via the Librosa library. The results demonstrate that the SVM model, when combined with constant data augmentation and MFCC extraction using Librosa, achieved the highest accuracy of 95.57%, highlighting its superior performance in Phonics alphabet spelling recognition.

articleTitle: Optimal Feature Set Analysis for Enhanced IoT Malware Detection with RFE and XGBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The swift integration of various industries through the Internet of Things (IoT) has escalated concerns about security, particularly regarding malware that has the potential to either exfiltrate data or interfere with operations. Numerous malware detection models have been developed; however, a significant concern remains the lack of emphasis on the speed at which threats can be detected. This paper introduces a malware detection model that combines choosing important features, balancing data, and machine learning. By examining the optimal number of features using a heuristic approach, the model can enhance detection speed without sacrificing the detection performance. Additionally, balancing techniques can address issues arising from uneven data distribution. The model classifies IoT traffic using XGBoost and is measured by six metrics: AUC, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and execution time. Results show that using 11 features can classified data in 2.22 seconds, with 99.9952% AUC, 99.8106% precision, 99.8064% recall, 99.8064% F1-score, and 99.8048% accuracy.

articleTitle: Melon Fruit Quality Classification with Hyperparameter Optimization of Random Forest Algorithm Using Grey Wolf Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Machine vision technology has significantly transformed the agricultural sector, particularly fruit classification. Accurate melon classification helps maintain product quality, enhances the supply chain, and reduces waste. Traditionally, determining fruit quality classification was done manually by farmers, which often required time and effort. This study optimizes the hyperparameters of the Random Forest algorithms using Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) by combining color features extraction from histograms and texture features from the Grey Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM). The use of GWO significantly improved the precision of the Random Forest algorithm to 92.43%, with hyperparameter optimization on n_estimators, max_features, and max_depth affecting the overall model performance. Consequently, this research makes a valuable contribution to improving the efficiency of melon quality classification through more effective hyperparameter optimization.

articleTitle: Polarization-Affinity of Indonesian Political Figures: Insights from Network of Twitter Followers with Modularity Clustering and Linear Arrangement
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This study investigates political polarization in Indonesia using Twitter follower networks of political figures. This is particularly evident in interactions on social media, primarily through followers of political accounts on Twitter. The more users who follow figures or media from a single political spectrum, the higher the level of polarization among followers, indicating a tendency to be exposed to one-sided political views. This study utilizes a dataset of the Twitter accounts of Indonesian political figures and their followers. We applied modularity clustering and minimum linear arrangement to reveal patterns of political affiliation and polarization. Subsequently, Minimum Linear Arrangement is employed to organize and visualize these groups, providing a more structured view of political affinity distribution within the network. This approach offers deep insights into how followers of political accounts are fragmented along the political spectrum and illustrates the level of polarization among supporters of political figures. Our findings highlight fragmented communities along the political spectrum, with modularity clustering scoring 0.20. The findings of this study also analyze political affinity based on Twitter follower data, offering a basis for understanding potential voter engagement and public participation in elections through digital platforms.

articleTitle: Multi-Purpose Security Camera for E-Cigarette Smoke Detection with Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Smoke detection with alarm sensors is often less effective because it has a limited range and cannot distinguish cigarette smoke, vaping, or other types of smoke. At the same time, semantic segmentation offers a more comprehensive solution for detecting cigarette and e-cigarette smoke. However, detecting e-cigarette smoke specifically using semantic segmentation presents a research opportunity. To address this issue, this study proposes a new approach for detecting cigarette and e-cigarette smoke based on the shape of the smoke using semantic segmentation with the lightweight DeepLabv3 architecture and MobileNetV2 backbone. First, we downloaded the smoke semantic segmentation dataset from Kaggle called “GOES16 Wildfires Smoke Plumes Dataset”. Then, we designed and tested the semantic segmentation with the DeepLabv3 model and compared J-statistics and G-mean optimization. In the next step, we developed a multi-purpose security camera design that can perform surveillance while detecting e-cigarette smoke in a certain area. Finally, we tested our semantic segmentation model on several e-cigarette smoke images and several images that did not contain e-cigarette smoke. We use several metrics, such as sensitivity, specificity, dice, and pixel accuracy. The test results show that the ROC from the training results of the semantic segmentation model on the smoke dataset has an AUC of 0.90. J-statistics and G-mean produce two different optimum threshold values, 0.52 and 0.55, respectively. It turns out that the optimized model with a threshold from G-mean has better sensitivity, dice, and pixel accuracy values than J-statistics, with values of 0.80, 0.85, 0.86, and 0.77, respectively.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Transformer Models for Bird Song Recognition Using Mel-Spectrograms
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This study explores the application of Vision Transformer (ViT), Data-efficient Image Transformer (DeiT), and Swin Transformer models for bird species classification using mel-spectrogram representations of bird songs. The research utilized the BirdClef 2024 dataset, consisting of 24,641 audio recordings across 182 bird species. The dataset was processed into mel-spectrograms and split into training, validation, and test sets to evaluate model performance. Each model was trained over 75 epochs with early stopping mechanisms in place. The results indicated strong training accuracy for all three models; however, validation accuracy plateaued between 78% and 84%, revealing overfitting issues. To address these challenges, various optimizations were implemented, including advanced learning rate scheduling, targeted dropout rates, weight decay adjustments, and data augmentation techniques. Despite these modifications, some overfitting persisted, particularly in the DeiT model, which showed decreased test accuracy after optimization. These findings highlight the effectiveness of transformer-based models for audio-based bird species classification, while also underscoring the need for further regularization techniques and fine-tuning. Future work should focus on exploring additional transformer architectures, refining regularization methods, and utilizing larger datasets to enhance model generalization and accuracy in complex classification tasks.

articleTitle: Personalize E-Commerce Product Recommendations Based on User Behavior Using Reinforced Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The development of a personalized and adaptive e-commerce product recommendation system will be developed using the Reinforcement Learning algorithm in this study. Initial data is extremely promising in its ability to raise sales conversion: 30% of the products added to the cart are never purchased. Additionally, there is a strong correlation of 0.8 between viewed versus purchased products. Data collection was from 447 Indonesian respondents over a period of June to July 2024. It was collected using an online questionnaire that measures recommendation quality, satisfaction, and ease of use with purposive sampling. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling was done on the data analysis. From that, it has been found that system quality is positively related to the accuracy, novelty, and diversity of the recommendation. The results further show how this would lead to an improved user experience, satisfaction, and sales conversion with the reinforcement learning-based system. These findings give insight into developing efficient adaptive recommendation systems on e-commerce platforms and open opportunities for further research.

articleTitle: Exploring Deep Object Content through In-hand Tactile Vibration Sensing with Shaking Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with insights beyond visual limitations, enabling the detection of surface characteristics and deformation properties like texture and slip. However, identifying internal content conditions remains a challenge. This study introduces a tactile-driven approach for classifying the internal content of various containers through vibration sensing and controlled shaking manipulation. By dynamically altering the mass distribution within the object, the system generates distinct changes in the center of mass (CoM), resulting in unique vibrational patterns. These patterns are captured and processed by a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to categorize the content state as depleted, partially loaded, or maximally loaded. Experimental results demonstrate a classification accuracy of 93 %, with clear clustering of content conditions, validating the effectiveness of this tactile-based approach across different fill levels. This tactile-based method significantly enhances robotic perception in tasks requiring internal content knowledge, such as sorting, recycling, and storage, offering a robust and scalable solution for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Normality Shift Identification for Anomaly Detection of Windows Event Logs
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Anomaly detection in network traffic is becoming increasingly difficult with increasing network complexity. Deep learning-based models, such as Autoencoder, are widely used to detect anomalies in normal data. However, when there is a shift in normality, these models fail to recognize new data patterns. This study highlights the importance of overcoming such challenges, particularly in Windows event logs, where changes in data distribution can cause anomaly detection failure. This study focuses on identifying normality shift in Windows event logs and overcomes the limitations of asymmetric Kullback-Leibler Divergence (KLD) using symmetric Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) and Hellinger Distance (HD). The proposed method can measure distribution differences more evenly and accurately. The experimental results demonstrate that normality shift affect model performance. The performance of the anomaly detection model improved after testing the data distribution and filtering out outliers or anomalies that caused the distribution shift. KLD and JSD detect shift in the ranges of 0.0-0.2, 0.4-0.6, and 0.8-1.0. However, JSD detects less shift than KLD due to its symmetrical nature. The HD method more accurately detected shift after filtering because of its sensitivity to small differences in both distributions.

articleTitle: Various Signal Transformation for Optimizing CNN Model Performance of Earthquake Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Given the frequency of earthquakes in Indonesia, it is crucial to accurately identify them in order to prevent unnecessary alarms over their mitigation. In the context of earthquake detection and classification, the development of artificial intelligence is ongoing to achieve a dependable system. The objective of this work is to compare the signal transformations as a preprocessing step in order to achieve optimal performance outcomes for the deep learning model in detecting seismic signals. The signal transformations used in this study are Fourier, wavelet, Hilbert, and probability of power spectral density (PPSD) methods to obtain a visual representation of the signal spectrum. The unprocessed data obtained from the Indonesia Tsunami Early Warning System (InaTEWS) server underwent a classification process including three distinct categories: earthquake, background noise, and instrument noise. Seismic signal identification is performed by utilizing the signal spectrum obtained from preprocessing the raw data on the optimized convolutional neural network (CNN) model. The assessment revealed that PPSD represents the optimal signal transformation approach, achieving a peak accuracy of 97.2% under RMSprop optimization, whereas Adam optimization exhibits slightly superior precision and F1 scores of 97.3 % and 97.2 %, respectively. It is believed that these favorable results will improve the dependability of the earthquake detection system based on artificial intelligence, therefore minimizing the occurrence of detection errors that may result in public widespread panic and chaos.

articleTitle: Diploma Verification Through Multi-Modal Image Processing: Face Detection, Perforation Text Recognition, and System Architecture Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This research presents a novel approach to digitally verify diploma authenticity using a combination of Siamese Neural Network (SNN) for face verification and YOLOv8 for text perforation detection. The SNN model, utilizing a binary cross-entropy loss function, successfully minimized the loss value from 0.169 to 0.0025 by the sixtieth epoch, achieving an accuracy of 0.98. This demonstrates the model's high proficiency in differentiating between anchor and positive/negative images. Additionally, the YOLOv8 model achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.93 at a 0.5 IoU threshold, further enhancing the precision of text perforation detection. This integrated system offers a robust and efficient method for ensuring the authenticity of diploma documents, contributing significantly to digital document security and forgery prevention. The research supports the implementation of deep learning in official document verification.

articleTitle: An Autonomic Computing Based Secure Password Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Passwords have become an essential part of everyday life for the average Internet user. As data breaches and website compromises become more common, securing user credentials during web browsing has become more crucial than ever. While most users know that their passwords have been compromised, filtering through hundreds of accounts manually does not inspire a will to change the said passwords. The literature review examines statistics related to password breaches, emphasizing the likelihood of users reusing passwords across multiple sites and the frequency with which users change passwords following a breach. In this paper we are presenting the design of a Chrome extension that checks if a user's credentials have been compromised upon reaching a log in screen. In case the user's credentials have been found in a breach, the extension offers advice and a strong memorable password. The autonomic manager utilizes a well-known API to access a continuously updated list of compromised websites, enabling real-time comparison of captured credentials. Through this approach, users are supplied with timely information to encourage them to change and create stronger passwords on compromised websites, thereby enhancing the security of their online interactions.

articleTitle: In-Silico Pipelined Medical Compound Generation for Neglected Tropical Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs) continue to pose significant health burdens in impoverished regions worldwide. Despite their impact, pharmaceutical investment in developing treatments for NTDs remains limited, largely due to the resource-intensive nature of traditional drug discovery methods. The framework employs Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) integrated with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to generate novel drug compounds. These compounds are then subjected to a comprehensive evaluation process, including screening through Lipinski's Rule of Five for oral bioavailability, Tanimoto Similarity analysis for structural comparison with existing NTD drugs, and Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship (QSAR) modeling to predict medical potency. The results demonstrated that the proposed GAN-LSTM model successfully generated 100,000 novel compounds, of which 84.45% were identified as valid molecules based on Lipinski's Rule of Five. The generated compounds exhibited Tanimoto similarity scores ranging from 0.1448 to 0.75, with an average of 0.5102 for valid compounds, indicating a balance between novelty and similarity to existing NTD drugs. To validate the efficacy of the approach, the researchers compared it to a benchmark model using only LSTM-based RNNs, which generated only 56.46% valid molecules from the same number of samples. This comparison further underscores the potential of the GAN-enhanced generative AI approach to substantially expedite the drug discovery pipeline for NTD treatments, offering a promising pathway to address these long-neglected health challenges more efficiently and effectively.

articleTitle: Improved Small Object Detection with YOLOv8 in Remote Sensing Imagery: Architecture Modifications and Loss Function Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Remote sensing's ability to identify small objects is essential for earth observation, but algorithms developed for remote sensing remain challenged in achieving high accuracy. This research addresses critical challenges in remote sensing, including the small size of objects relative to the entire image, random object orientations requiring rotation-invariant detection, and significant variations in object scale. Furthermore, the model effectively handles noise occlusions and demonstrates the effectiveness of the Wise Intersection over Union (WIoU) loss function in improving performance and robustness. This research proposed a modified YOLOv8 model by replacing the C2f layer with the C3 layer, adding layers to the neck, and adding a head component. However, the modified model underperforms when using the Complete Intersection over Union (CIoU) loss function, achieving mean Average Precision (mAP) of 76.146% accuracy due to increased complexity, causing noisier predictions. In contrast, applying the WIoU loss function improves the model's performance, achieving an mAP of 77.183% accuracy and an improvement of 0.875% over the base model by better handling prediction variability.

articleTitle: Predictive Maintenance on Milling Machines Using Long Short-Term Memory and Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, predictive maintenance has become a key strategy to improve the reliability and efficiency of industrial equipment by anticipating potential failures. This study develops and implements machine learning models to predict the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of machinery and classify machine conditions for predictive maintenance. Using multi-sensor data, including air temperature, process temperature, rotational speed, torque, and tool wear-this research integrates Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models. The LSTM model handles time-series data to predict RUL, while the SVM model classifies machinery conditions based on features derived from LSTM outputs. An experimental approach with quantitative analysis divides the data into training and testing sets to validate model performance. Metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC (Area Under Curve) evaluate the models' effectiveness in predicting failures and classifying conditions. Results show that the combination of LSTM and SVM improves predictive maintenance accuracy, facilitating better repair scheduling and reducing unplanned downtime. This study provides valuable insights into the practical use of machine learning in industrial settings, advancing smart manufacturing and data-driven maintenance strategies.
